# Tests the dashboard cites as evidence for a "verified" guarantee or a
# "pass" attack, and that windows-latest legitimately SKIPs rather than
# fails or passes -- read by .github/scripts/assert-evidence-ran.sh's
# optional second argument. This file changes nothing for linux or macos:
# they invoke that script with one argument, and this one is not built.
#
# Every entry here traces to the same root cause, in one of two shapes:
#
#   Holdcall never implemented a kernel-verified peer identity for Windows'
#   AF_UNIX (afunix.sys has no peer-credentials call, and Holdcall does not
#   use the peer pid it can report), and said so rather than ship an
#   unverified one -- see
#   engine/internal/peer/peer_windows.go and image_windows.go. Production
#   code treats "unsupported" as "not a denial" for the accept check
#   (daemon.go) and for decisions (shim.go's daemonIsGenuine), which is a
#   real, documented, known limitation (docs/security.md), not a testing gap
#   -- these tests exist to prove an attacker is refused, and on this
#   platform today it is not. It is a denial where a secret is concerned: a
#   credential is never released to a peer that cannot be verified, nor a
#   connector's command taken from a daemon that cannot be, and the windows
#   tests that show that are not in this list because they run and pass.
#
#   Agent enrolment (peer.ImageOfFile) is an admitted stub on Windows for
#   the same reason: an unverified identity mechanism is worse than an
#   absent one (image_windows.go). Enrolling a real file cannot succeed
#   there.
#
# Each t.Skip site names this file and its reason inline; this list is
# what makes the CI gate that would otherwise catch a skip honest about it.

TestDeriveAgentMatchesTheEnrolledParent	peer.ParentOf is unsupported on windows (peer_windows.go); the test's own t.Skipf fires before it can enrol anything to match against
TestTwoRealAgentsAgainstOneConnectorReceiveDifferentVerdicts	agent derivation (peer.ParentOf/ImageOf) is unsupported on windows; deriveAgent always returns "" there, so two agents cannot be told apart
TestANonNimProcessCannotWriteToTheJournal	daemon.go refuses a peer only when supported && !isSelf; peer.IsSelf reports unsupported on windows, so an unverified peer is let through rather than refused
TestANonNimProcessCannotObtainADecision	same as above: the accept-time peer check does not refuse an unverified caller on windows, so the daemon would actually answer it
TestAnImpostorOnTheSocketCannotChooseWhatIsSpawned	daemonIsGenuine (shim.go) is "!supported || isSelf"; on windows peer.IsSelf is always unsupported, so an impostor daemon is treated as genuine instead of refused
TestAnImpostorLearnsNothingFromTheAttempt	same daemonIsGenuine gap: on windows the shim would talk to the impostor rather than refuse it
TestAnImpostorCannotDecideCalls	same daemonIsGenuine gap: on windows the shim would accept a decision from the impostor rather than refuse it
TestDialDaemonRefusesAnImpostor	same daemonIsGenuine gap: DialDaemon would hand back a connection to the impostor on windows instead of refusing it
TestAPathSwapDoesNotDefeatPeerIdentity	peer identity is unsupported on windows by design; IsSelf reports supported=false, so the property this test demonstrates cannot be shown there
TestAReplacedFileIsReportedStaleRatherThanFailing	agent enrolment resolves identity via peer.ImageOfFile, which always errors on windows (image_windows.go); enrolling the file this test needs already fails before it can go stale
TestTheDaemonsCommandIsSpawnedNotTheCallersEndToEnd	fixture hardcodes /bin/echo and /bin/sh -c, neither of which exists at that path on windows; and on windows the relay takes no connector from a daemon it cannot verify (shim.injectionFromAnswer), so there is no injection to check -- TestOnWindowsARelayDoesNotSpawnWhatAnUnverifiedDaemonNamed checks the refusal instead
TestWithNoConnectorTheCallersCommandRuns	fixture hardcodes /bin/echo, which does not exist at that path on windows; not a peer-identity gap, a fixture one
TestStatusDoesNotCallAnImpostorTheDaemon	peer identity is unsupported on windows, so status cannot tell an impostor apart there; the same gap the Known gaps table records
TestAnInPlaceUpgradeIsDiagnosedAndDaemonRestartFixesIt	peer identity is unsupported on windows, so an older build cannot be told apart from anything; and holdcall daemon restart is not supported there
TestADefaultDenyClosesEverythingAndAnAgentScopedAllowReopensOneToolForOneAgent	agent enrolment resolves identity via peer.ImageOfFile, which always errors on windows (image_windows.go); the agent-scoped allow this test proves cannot be set there
TestEnrolmentEntersTheChain	same enrolment gap: holdcall agent add fails on windows before anything can enter the chain
TestASecondNameForOneExecutableIsRefusedNamingTheFirst	same enrolment gap: the first enrolment already fails on windows, so there is no first name for a second to be refused against
